description:
## Goal (invariant, not pass/green)
A closure value has EXACTLY ONE physical transport layout, derived once from its construction (what it captures), and that layout is the single source of truth at every carrier -- entry, capture, continuation, call-arg. The demand/use axis describes what is READ; it must be structurally incapable of describing what is LAID OUT. Under this invariant two observers of one closure cannot disagree about its shape -- disagreement is unrepresentable, not merely un-triggered. The shared Enum.reduce* bridge over Range/Map settling is a CONSEQUENCE of this, not the target.

## Root cause (ground truth, HEAD 8a91e9c90, reduce/2 worked example)
For `Enum.reduce(1..7//2, fn (x, acc) -> x * acc end)`:
- Enum.reduce/2 (fn 67) builds inner lambda L = `fn (entry, state) -> reduce_first_step(entry, state, reducer) end` (FunctionId 174), capturing the user reducer. The closure record physically holds ONE capture slot (the boxed reducer callable); its canonical interned descr.capture_shapes = [Callable].
- reduce_first_step/3 (fn 114) splits on `state`: `(entry, :first, _reducer)` IGNORES the reducer; `(entry, {:acc, acc}, reducer)` CALLS it. So L specializes into activation A (state = :first sentinel) and B (state = {:acc,_} tuple).
- Activation A's reducer-capture input (sem0) is anchored by TWO transport passes that DISAGREE:
  - seed-callable-flow-capture-inputs (transport.rs:1710): derives capture shape from the consuming activation's backward USE-demand via shape_for_local_value. On the :first path nothing reads the reducer -> demand bottoms to Ignore -> ShapeId Nothing.
  - seed_callable_resolution_capture_inputs (transport.rs:1738): derives it from the closure's canonical descr.capture_shapes -> ShapeId Callable.
  - Nothing vs Callable for the SAME capture slot of the SAME closure value -> component_shapes agree-or-panic meet (transport.rs:338) fires.
The defect is that a USE-demand axis can manufacture a layout (Nothing) that contradicts the closure's construction layout (Callable). That violates [[feedback_shapeid_is_pure_layout]]: transport ShapeId is physical layout, not use/contract.

## Required work (correct-by-construction; the removal IS the fix)
- Make a closure's capture-input layout a SINGLE construction-derived fact owned by the value. The use-demand path that derives a capture-input shape (transport.rs:1710 via shape_for_local_value) is DELETED, not reconciled with the canonical path -- there must be exactly one seeder of capture-input shapes. Caveat to resolve first: the canonical descr pass (1738) only fires for function-identified closures (descr.function == Some); boxed callables (function: None) currently rely on 1710. The single canonical seeder must therefore cover boxed-callable resolutions too, or the deletion strands them. This gate is load-bearing.
- The agree-or-panic meet (transport.rs:338) should become unreachable by construction: either delete it or degrade it to a can't-happen assertion, since no path can anchor two shapes to one closure value once layout has a single source.
- The use-demand axis must remain incapable of producing a layout for ANY carrier of a captured callable (value, call-arg), not just capture-inputs -- verify no sibling site re-introduces Nothing-vs-Callable one position over.
- Remove the stale defer.* flags from fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar (already settles on HEAD; its presence is now noise).

## Signal (property, not fixture-green)
Assert the invariant directly, loud at the source: every capture-input position's transport shape equals its closure's construction-layout shape, suite-wide. A future divergence must fire WHERE the layout is decided, not as a downstream meet panic or a native-callable-boundary-multiplicity error.

## bfh.4 / to_list Range+Map (same invariant, one stage downstream -- to CONFIRM)
to_list Range+Map fails at native lowering with 'native callable materialization matched multiple native boundaries' for the same bridge lambda. Hypothesis: native materialization cannot pick one boundary precisely BECAUSE the closure presents more than one layout -- the same single-layout invariant violated downstream. Confirm this is the same root once the invariant holds; if a distinct invariant is broken, file it as its own ticket (do not fold silently).

## NOT the problem (superseded)
The earlier framing (non-monotone return-ascent storm; make surface/return joins monotone) does NOT reproduce on HEAD -- f98.1/f98.2 already settled convergence; define_return already treats None as a no-op bottom on the join path. No storm exists. The fix is closure capture-layout identity in transport.

comments.text: INVESTIGATION CHECKPOINT (not yet implemented). Ground truth confirmed: f98.2's addressed-frame surface match is already correct -- runtime_demand.rs:519-522 compares own_surface (past captures) to surface.inputs and skips on mismatch, NOT a raw-slot compare. So f98.3's locus is the RETURN-EVIDENCE join, not the surface match. Per f98's pinned telemetry (~52941 activation_analysis re-derivations paired 1:1 with return_type; #1 oscillator Enum.reduce fn69; churning Map-reduce callsite with return_ty: None on Ty(19) -- same fn/type as fz-bfh.3's absent value), the storm is a NON-MONOTONE RETURN ASCENT: the shared bridge executable's return type drops back to None rather than widening monotonically once concrete evidence arrives ([[unknown-is-not-none]] / convergence-by-construction). FIX SHAPE (Output Contract Loop, fresh budget): (1) reproduce the range+map storm with the fz-bfh.7 JobBudgetGuard to name the oscillating kind loud; (2) trace to the exact site where the bridge return_ty is RE-GROUND to None instead of joined; (3) make the join widen-only -- absent stays None, proven-empty stays none(), concrete ascends by union only -- and DELETE the re-grounding (the 'remove what's no longer necessary'); (4) regression: range+map reduce/to_list compiles within the normal drive budget with bounded activation_analysis/return_type churn (guard-observed), ReturnType widening telemetry NOT the escape hatch. Did NOT implement at this session's context depth to avoid the sprawl class we just cleaned (see fz-bfh.5.5 history).

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (ran the three deferred fixtures with defers stripped on HEAD 8a91e9c90 — ground truth, not the stale pinned telemetry the prior checkpoint relied on):

NO STORM EXISTS. The semantic drive converges. The prior 'non-monotone return-ascent storm' hypothesis does NOT reproduce: a range+map reduce/3 probe reaches semantic closure AND transport in <4k jobs, and define_return already treats None as a no-op bottom on the join path. The ~52941 figure was a pre-f98.1/.2 measurement; f98.1 (pin reduce bridge callable contract) + f98.2 (keep boundary surfaces authoritative) already settled the convergence.

Actual current state of the three regression targets:
- fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar (bfh.1, reduce/3 over Range): ALL THREE PATHS PASS. Its defer.* flags are STALE and should be removed.
- fz_f98_range_reduce2 (bfh.2, reduce/2 over stepped Range): FAILS at transport.rs:338 — 'transport shape anchors disagree for connected position component'. The shared bridge reducer FunctionId(174) input0 is anchored to BOTH ShapeId(11) and ShapeId(14) within one connected union component (equalities cite transport.rs:1423/1887/1935). A shape-anchor conflict, NOT a return-ascent oscillation.
- fz_f98_range_map_converges (bfh.4, to_list Range+Map): FAILS at native lowering — 'native callable materialization for FunctionId(174)/0 matched multiple native boundaries' (e.g. [NativeCallableBoundaryId(8),(11)] for one published BoundaryId(21)). Same root cause one layer down: the shared bridge callable resolves to MULTIPLE boundaries.

REVISED LOCUS: the live defect is the shared bridge (FunctionId(174)) carrying MULTIPLE callable shapes/boundaries at ONE published transport position — the bfh.2 'multi-surface callable value resolved by native pick-first instead of producer identity' problem, surfacing as (a) conflicting transport ShapeId anchors and (b) multiple native boundaries. The fix belongs in transport callable-boundary identity / shape anchoring, NOT in the semantic return join. Next: determine whether ShapeId(11) vs (14) are layout-identical (interning/identity fragmentation — see [[feedback_shapeid_is_pure_layout]]) or genuinely divergent layouts (bridge needs per-shape boundary identity). The prior monotone-return fix is moot and was NOT implemented (good — it would not have touched these failures).

DONE (commit c9baed811). Landed the construction-layout invariant for closure captures.

What landed:
- Collapsed the two capture-input seeders into ONE canonical seed_callable_capture_inputs (transport.rs) that derives a capture's shape from the closure's construction layout = the joined demand over ALL of the flow's resolutions, anchored identically for every resolution. Deleted the redundant descriptor-driven seed_callable_resolution_capture_inputs. Net removal.
- The use-demand axis can no longer manufacture a layout (Nothing) that contradicts the closure's construction layout (Callable); the shape-anchor disagreement is unrepresentable, not merely untriggered.
- Kept the transport.rs:338 agree-or-panic meet: it is already a can't-happen assertion with rich diagnostics and guards EVERY position component (general defense-in-depth), not capture-specific dead code -- deleting it would remove a real invariant check.
- Regression: compiler2_transport_plan_keeps_unused_capture_on_specialized_activation_at_construction_layout (transport_contract_test) drives reduce/2 over Range to a transport plan and asserts capture inputs match the canonical descriptor. Verified RED without the fix (panics at transport.rs:338, ShapeId(11)=Nothing vs ShapeId(14)=Callable on the lambda capture), GREEN with it.
- Removed stale defer.* from fz_f98_range_reduce_scalar (reduce/3 over Range; passes all 3 matrix paths).

Verification: full lib failure set IDENTICAL to baseline (13 pre-existing reds, diffed by stashing the change) -> zero regressions, zero coincidental fixes; clippy 0 warnings; transport contract suite 56/0.

Distinct invariant breaks discovered and filed (NOT folded): fz-f98.6 (native callable boundary fragmentation: one published transport boundary -> multiple native boundaries; reproduces for a zero-capture bridge lambda so structurally outside this fix) and fz-f98.7 (reduce/2 :first|{:acc} accumulator does not thread back through the Range bridge -> Enum.EmptyError). fz_f98_range_reduce2 and fz_f98_range_map_converges stay deferred pointing at those tickets.

title: closure capture layout must not fragment on use-demand across specialized activations
